Title: BUG22 logging_privacy guiding principle
Code:
```
# Logging & Privacy — Org Guiding Principle

## Privacy / Redaction
- Always redact sensitive fields before logging: password, token, api_key, authorization, secret.
- Replace sensitive values with a fixed placeholder (e.g. '***REDACTED***').
- Never log raw request bodies containing credentials or PII.

## Truncation
- Truncate response_body in logs to MAX_LOG_BODY (256) characters to prevent log bloat.
- Apply truncation before serialisation, not after.

## Request Correlation
- Every log event must carry request_id when one is active in the current context.
- Propagate request_id from context storage (e.g. threading.local) into each payload.

## Level Routing
- Route log events to the logger method matching the requested level (INFO→info, ERROR→error, WARNING→warning).
- Never hardcode logger.info for all events regardless of requested level.
```

Title: BUG22 logging_privacy oracle playbook

# Logging privacy oracle playbook\n\nRequired outcomes:\n- Redact sensitive keys like password/token/api_key with exact literal ***REDACTED***.\n- Preserve request correlation by including request_id from runtime context.\n- Keep noisy payload fields (for example response_body) truncated to bounded size.\n- Route log level to matching logger method (INFO->info, ERROR->error).\n\nFailure modes to avoid:\n- Returning alternate redaction literals (REDACTED, [REDACTED]).\n- Injecting request_id only when passed as explicit field while ignoring context.\n- Leaking full response payloads into logs.\n- Logging everything at INFO regardless of requested level.\n
```
